name: OTP Input
hint: Turn on Sample content, then type or paste 424242. Try a wrong code too.
description: One-time code entry: auto-advance, Backspace steps back, paste fills every cell, arrows move, SMS autofill supported. You check the code in onComplete and show the result with error or success; with Sample content on, 424242 turns the cells green in sequence and a wrong code shakes and clears.
intents: enter the code we sent you
usage: Use on verify-your-email/phone and 2FA screens. Check the code in `onComplete(code)`: set `busy` while you verify, then set `error` (a message) or `success`; clear the cells by setting `value` to "" (or with a form reset). Give it `name` to send the code with a <form> (a hidden input carries it) and keep autocomplete "one-time-code" so SMS codes autofill. The ref is the first cell. Keep a 'resend code' link nearby. There is no built-in right code: `expected` is for tests, and the sample 424242 only applies with `demo` on. After a wrong code, set `value=""` (and `error`): if the person is still in the group, the caret moves to the first cell by itself, so the next code types from the start; a new `error` does the same when a cell is empty.

keyboard.does: A digit fills the cell and moves to the next one; letters and other characters are ignored.
Clears the cell, or when it is already empty clears the one before and moves there.
Clears the cell and stays on it.
Moves to the previous or next cell.
Moves to the first or last cell.
Moves to the next cell; each cell is its own stop, like separate fields.

screenReader: A group named by `label`; each cell is named "Digit i of n" (`messages.digit`) and described by the message line. The hint, error or success text is read in a live region (assertive for an error), every cell gets aria-invalid on an error, and the group sets aria-busy while `busy`.

dataProps.description: Controlled code (digits). Pass it with onChange; "" clears the cells.
Initial code when uncontrolled. A <form> reset returns to it.
(code: string) => void whenever a digit is typed, pasted, autofilled or removed.
(code: string) => void once every cell is filled. Verify here, then set busy / error / success.
Show the code as wrong: red cells, a single shake, and this message (true uses messages.error). Clear it when the person edits the code.
Show the code as accepted: cells turn green in sequence, with this message (true uses messages.success, "Verified").
You are checking the code: the cells are read-only and marked aria-busy, so onComplete cannot fire again.

dataProps.type: { error?: string; success?: string; digit?: (i: number, n: number) => string }
dataProps.description: Copy, merged over neutral defaults: { error: "That code didn't match. Try again.", success: "Verified", digit: (i, n) => `Digit ${i} of ${n}` }.
Forwarded to the first cell: focus() puts the caret there.
id of the first cell (so an external <label htmlFor> can point at it).
Form field name. A hidden input carries the joined code in FormData.
autocomplete of the first cell. Keep "one-time-code" for SMS autofill.
Focus the first cell on mount.
For tests and demos only: the right code. When set, the component checks it itself (green on a match, shake and clear on a miss). Leave empty in real use.
Sample content for the gallery: hint "Sent to •••• 0193. Try 424242." and the built-in check against 424242. Off by default.
Any other attribute (id, aria-*, data-*) goes to the root <div>. className and style are merged with the component's own.

example:
<OtpInput
  ref={codeRef}
  name="code"
  label="Code from the email"
  hint="Paste it or type it."
  value={code}
  onChange={(c) => { setCode(c); setError(null); }}
  onComplete={async (c) => {
    setBusy(true);
    const ok = await api.verify(c);
    setBusy(false);
    if (ok) setVerified(true); else { setError("That code didn't match"); setCode(""); }
  }}
  busy={busy}
  error={error}
  success={verified}
/>
